definitions.explanation: A container used for packing and carrying a boxed meal ({弁当|べんとう}). Comes in various materials and styles, from simple plastic to elaborate lacquerware.

examples.japanese: {弁当箱|べんとうばこ}を{洗|あら}う。
{新|あたら}しい{弁当箱|べんとうばこ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a new lunch box.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{弁当箱|べんとうばこ}に{好|す}きなキャラクターの{絵|え}が{描|えが}いてある。
examples.english: My child's lunch box has pictures of their favorite character on it.

notes:
A compound of {弁当|べんとう} (boxed lunch) + {箱|はこ} (box). An everyday item in Japanese life, as many people bring homemade {弁当|べんとう} to school or work.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弁当箱|べんとうばこ}を{詰|つ}める: to pack a lunch box
- {弁当箱|べんとうばこ}を{洗|あら}う: to wash the lunch box
- {二段|にだん}{弁当箱|べんとうばこ}: two-tier lunch box
- {保温|ほおん}{弁当箱|べんとうばこ}: insulated lunch box

TYPES:
Japanese lunch boxes come in many styles:
- {曲|まげ}わっぱ: traditional bentwood lunch box
- {重箱|じゅうばこ}: stacking lacquer boxes (used for おせち and special occasions)
- ステンレス{製|せい}: stainless steel type

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {弁当箱|べんとうばこ} are not just functional containers. Many parents take pride in making attractive, character-themed lunches ({キャラ弁|きゃらべん}) for their children.
